subject: Velox Health — inflight streaming freeze and WebSocket handshake timeouts
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@veloxhealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@veloxhealth.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 08:42:15 -0800
Subject: Realtime API - streaming stalls / chunked transfers stalling since 08:40 PT

Markus —

We're seeing a customer-impacting issue starting ~08:40 PT where streaming responses over our integration with Redwood suddenly stop emitting tokens mid-response. The client request stays open for 20–45s with no data, then the connection either times out (we see WebSocket handshake/timeouts) or returns partial output. Metrics this morning vs baseline: error rate up ~5pp, median tail latency for first token ~1.5s (usually ~200ms), and throughput for the realtime endpoint increased ~2.4x due to a marketing spike.

Sample request ids attached (velox_sample_request_11-18.log). We're also seeing chunked transfer stalls (no chunks for 10–30s) and intermittent 502/504 from the proxy. This is affecting our conversational UI (conversion rate down visibly in the last hour).

Can you confirm if you have any immediate mitigations? We need a plan and ETA — this is impacting our production users.

—Sam
VP Product, Velox Health

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@veloxhealth.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 08:49:02 -0800
Subject: Re: Realtime API - streaming stalls / chunked transfers stalling since 08:40 PT

Sam — thanks for the quick heads up and logs. I'm escalating this to infra/ops immediately (cc Soojin).

Immediate asks from our side so we can act quickly:
- Can you confirm the client connection type (WebSocket vs. EventStream) for the impacted requests?
- Are you able to reproduce with a small test token stream we provide?

Short-term mitigations I'm initiating now:
- Ask ops to enable a short keepalive/heartbeat (5s) and reduce proxy buffer coalescing to force chunk flushing.
- If you can tolerate a non-streaming response temporarily, toggle to the non-streaming fallback (we can help with a quick config flip).
- I'll set up a 30-minute call in 10 minutes to triage and will follow with an internal war-room if needed.

Attaching placeholder for logs we received (velox_sample_request_11-18.log).

I'll follow up with a consolidated plan once infra confirms the change.

—Markus
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Velox Health <sam.patel@veloxhealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:05:11 -0800
Subject: Re: Realtime API - streaming stalls / chunked transfers stalling since 08:40 PT

Triage notes (initial):
- Observed elevated counts of upstream 504 and WebSocket TIMEOUT events from the edge proxy starting 08:38–08:41 PT correlated with Velox request ids.
- Proxy (nginx edge) is coalescing small writes into larger chunks under current buffering config; under burst traffic that appears to be causing >10s gaps between flushed frames for some connections.
- We also see intermittent KB-sized frames being held during the handshake -> suspected buffer/coalescing + keepalive suppression.

Immediate plan executed:
1) Pushed a temporary proxy config change: reduce proxy_buffer_size and set proxy_send_timeout=25s; enabled application-level heartbeat every 5s for the route. Config diff attached (ops-proxy-config-diff.patch).
2) Created a canary route to markus-dedicated-velox with a dedicated GPU pool (low-latency profile) — will route 5% of traffic to verify stability.
3) Enabled extra websocket-level metrics (packet gaps, last-write delta) and started a short trace of 20 sample sessions.

Next steps: monitor for 30 minutes, if the canary looks stable we'll shift 30% of traffic and then open for general. If not, fall back to forcing non-streaming responses for impacted sessions.

Point of contact on ops: soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com — I'll post live updates to the incident channel.

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:18:04 -0800
Subject: Executive summary and customer communication — Velox incident

Team — cc'ing Rishi for visibility. Quick executive notes for customer/leadership:
- Customer: Velox Health, strategic account; renewal decision window ~early Dec. Production user impact being reported (conversion drop called out).
- Severity: High — streaming tokens stalling / Socket handshake/timeout causing visible UI drop.
- Asks: prepare a one-page incident brief for Velox and an internal 2-slide board summary within 2 hours. Include expected root-cause possibilities and the mitigation timeline.

Customer communication guidance:
- Be transparent: what we saw, what we changed (proxy buffer send-time, heartbeat), and next steps with ETA for RCA.
- Offer a provisional credit for the impacted window; we can finalize percentage after RCA.

Please prioritize this over other low-impact tickets. Markus — can you draft the customer-facing blurb I can review and send by 10:00 PT?

—Vanessa
Head of Customer Success — Redwood Inference

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@veloxhealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@veloxhealth.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 10:02:28 -0800
Subject: Re: Executive summary and customer communication — Velox incident

Thanks Markus / Soojin / Vanessa —

We confirmed the affected clients were using WebSocket-based streaming. After your temporary change we saw a big improvement for canary traffic (token gaps reduced). We're flipping affected sessions to the canary route now. We also toggled a short-term polling fallback for a subset of users to eliminate UI stalls while you monitor.

Impact note for internal: our product analytics show a ~12% dip in conversions on the affected experience during the window, so this will be material for our renewal conversation. We're grateful for the quick mitigation — please keep us posted on the RCA and the proposed credit.

I'll join the incident call at 10:15 PT. Attaching one more trace and a screenshot (velox_console_screenshot_11-18.png).

—Sam

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@veloxhealth.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-incident update and next steps — Velox Health streaming stall (initial)

All — quick consolidated update after today's triage and mitigations.

What we observed: 
- Edge proxy buffer coalescing combined with increased burst concurrency led to delayed chunk flushes and occasional websocket handshake timeouts for affected sessions.
- Effect: token-stream gaps (10–45s) and elevated 502/504s surfaced as client-visible hangs.

Immediate actions taken (complete):
- Reduced proxy buffer size, set proxy_send_timeout=25s, and enabled 5s heartbeat to keep the connection alive and force chunk flushing.
- Created a canary dedicated route (5% -> 30%) to validate under load; canary currently stable for 90 minutes.
- As a fail-safe, enabled non-streaming fallback flag for the most sensitive workflows.

Metrics (so far): canary traffic token gaps reduced to baseline; error rate for the route dropped from +5pp to +0.6pp. We'll continue monitoring 24 hours for regression.

Next steps & timeline:
- Deep RCA (infra + runtime) to be completed by Nov 20 10:00 PT (postmortem invite: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFR-7893).
- Ops runbook update and permanent proxy tuning (target: Nov 19 EOD).
- Customer-facing incident brief and proposed provisional credit (10% for impacted window) being drafted — Vanessa to review customer blurb by 10:00 PT tomorrow.

Attachments: ops-proxy-config-diff.patch; incident trace (velox_sample_request_11-18.log).

If Velox would like a walkthrough of the mitigation and the postmortem, we'll schedule a 45-minute briefing. Thank you for the quick coordination and patience — we'll aim to have the formal RCA and final credit decision after the Nov 20 postmortem.

—Markus
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
